tasks.short: Book invoices and bank lines in AFAS.

today.trigger: PDFs land in the AP mailbox, a staffing agency closes its weekly hours, or Rabobank delivers the day's bank file.
steps: Save the invoice from Outlook or from one of the three agency portals.
Key creditor, invoice number, amount, VAT and site into AFAS Profit, or check a line a colleague just keyed.
Attach the PDF to the AFAS dossier.
Post the journal to creditors, debtors or the general ledger.
Export a list to Excel when a site manager wants a split the screen does not give.
drudgery: Retyping creditor, IBAN, invoice number and amount from a PDF
Saving the same document in the dossier and again on SharePoint
Clicking through a posting that is the same as last week's
today.time_sinks: Mondays, and the weeks the flex pool climbs toward 300, when three agencies send thick invoices and the same figures are keyed once into AFAS and again into Excel.

lenses.faster: Supplier, amount, VAT and invoice number are on the posting before anyone opens AFAS, so the daily keying round shrinks to the lines the match cannot finish.
lenses.autonomous: A new PDF in the AP mailbox, an approved agency-hour file, or a CAMT.053 from Rabobank starts the booking on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every site and every agency invoice would be in the ledger the week it arrives, with the PDF still on the dossier, including the busy weeks when the flex pool grows.
lenses.joy: Retyping headers is work nobody will miss. What people still want is the odd transport surcharge and the agency bill that does not match the approved hours.
lenses.options: When the match is weak, show up to five posting proposals from that supplier's history, each with ledger, site, cost centre and VAT code, and rank them by how often they were used.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains supplier defaults, match tolerances and exception reasons, and reviews the posting log, one layer above keying each invoice.
reach: Routine journals the Accountant now types to move a matched item into the right period.
The weekday feed of coded cost-centre actuals the FP&A Analyst now rebuilds from Excel exports.
Status of a single invoice, which site managers now ask finance to look up.

tasks.human_edge: Judgment on a first-time supplier, a mixed VAT bill (21 percent on one line, reverse charge on a cross-border transport line), and a warehouse damage credit that should not hit the month's cost as if it were a normal purchase.
tasks.pattern_why: A posting changes the ledger the close and the auditor rely on. Capture and matching can run on the structured fields; a person still clears first-time suppliers, unusual VAT and amounts outside tolerance before those entries count.

in_practice.trigger: A PDF arrives in the AP mailbox, an agency portal marks hours approved, or Rabobank delivers the CAMT.053.
steps: Read header, lines, VAT and IBAN into a staging table and attach the file to the supplier dossier.
Match supplier, purchase order or agency order, and open amount in AFAS.
Propose ledger, cost centre, site and VAT code.
Post straight through when the supplier, amount and VAT sit inside the signed-off tolerance.
Leave the rest on a queue the bookkeeper clears the same day.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves first-time suppliers, a VAT code that is not the supplier default, and any line outside tolerance. Payment release stays with the two Rabobank authorisers.
data_needed: Creditor card with default ledger, cost centre, site and VAT code
Open purchase orders or receipts where they exist
Agency order numbers and approved hours
Cost centre list per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo)
VAT codes in use: 21 percent, 9 percent, 0 percent, intra-community, reverse charge
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS journal audit trail, with the PDF on the dossier, and a copy of the exception log in the SharePoint month-close folder the Controller already uses.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit records purchase invoices, sales invoices and journals and stores the document on the creditor or debtor dossier.
Vic.ai reads supplier invoices and proposes the posting from history, leaving exceptions to a person.
What share of Noordhaven's transport surcharges and agency invoices would post untouched is untested.

risks: A wrong reverse-charge code on international transport flows into the VAT return.
The same invoice arrives by mail and via the agency portal and is booked twice.
A service account posts entries the external auditor cannot tie to a named person.
The PDF is stored outside the AFAS dossier and the seven-year retention file is incomplete.
Agency invoices name flex workers and rates; a wide queue or export spreads that personal data.
research_questions: What share of purchase invoices last quarter came from suppliers with an unchanged ledger and VAT code?
Which capture add-on, if any, is already licensed on this AFAS administration, and what did it post untouched in a sample month?
How many bookings are reversed or recoded during the close, and on which ledgers?
Do the three agency portals give a line file, or only a PDF?

tasks.short: Check amounts, VAT and ledger codes on each posting.

today.trigger: A posting is about to be saved, or a second look is asked for just before the payment run.
steps: Open the PDF and the AFAS line side by side.
Recalculate quantity times price, VAT and the invoice total.
Compare ledger, cost centre, site and VAT code with what that supplier usually receives.
Search for the same invoice number on open and paid items.
Correct the line or send it back when a figure or a code is off.
drudgery: Re-adding a total the PDF already shows
Confirming the same supplier VAT code on every invoice
Ticking a long agency or carrier invoice line by line
today.time_sinks: Carrier bills with many surcharges, and agency invoices in peak season, because a wrong cost centre or VAT code often surfaces only when the Accountant reviews the month.

lenses.faster: Totals, VAT, IBAN checksum, duplicate invoice number and cost-centre validity are checked before anyone opens the document. The bookkeeper opens the failures.
lenses.autonomous: Every captured invoice and every saved journal runs the same checks at entry and again when the payment proposal is built.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every agency hour-line would be checked against the approved order, and shifted cost centres would be caught in the week they were coded.
lenses.joy: Re-adding PDFs on a calculator is work nobody will miss. The conversation that remains is whether a waiting-hour surcharge is a real cost for that site.
lenses.options: On a failed code, show the two or three ledgers and VAT codes this supplier has used in the past year and the reason this line was rejected.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper writes the check rules and reads the weekly failure report, one layer above re-checking each invoice.
reach: The sample checks the Accountant prepares for the external auditor.
The uncoded-invoice and exception counts the Controller wants on the close checklist.
Cash-application mismatches the Credit and Collections Officer now finds by hand.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a failed check is a real error or a fair exception: a credit note that covers two invoices, mixed VAT on one transport bill, or a cost centre the site opened last week and has not yet sent to finance.
tasks.pattern_why: The checks are arithmetic, allowed code lists and match rules. The output is pass or fail with a reason code, and another person can recompute it. A model is only useful earlier, to read the PDF into fields.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice is captured or a journal is saved in AFAS.
steps: Recalculate line totals, VAT and the invoice total from the captured fields.
Check the invoice number against open and paid items for that creditor.
Check ledger, cost centre, site and VAT code against the supplier default and the allowed lists.
Compare the amount to the purchase order, the receipt or the approved agency order when one exists.
Write pass or a reason code, and route only failures to the bookkeeper.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper accepts or corrects each failure before the item can be paid. After the Controller signs the rule set, a clean pass needs no second look.
data_needed: VAT rates and the code list, including reverse charge and intra-community
Supplier default ledger, cost centre and VAT code
Open order and receipt amounts
Approved agency hours and order numbers
Cost centres per site
Duplicate window the Controller accepts
in_practice.logs_to: A check log in AFAS, summarised on the Power BI finance dashboard from the nightly extract.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit approval workflows can hold a purchase invoice until the assigned person releases it for payment.
Basware matches an invoice to an order and a receipt and flags lines outside tolerance.
Once the invoice is structured data, total, VAT and code-list checks are ordinary validation rules.

risks: Tolerances set too tight block every Friday payment run on fuel and toll invoices that never match to the cent.
Tolerances set too loose let a wrong VAT code into the return.
An 'accept all' habit on the failure queue turns the control into a rubber stamp.
Many invoices have no purchase order, so a three-way match on rent, utilities and agency bills will fail forever unless those rules differ.
research_questions: What are the ten most common reasons an invoice is corrected or sent back today?
What amount difference does the business already accept on transport surcharges?
Which checks does the external auditor sample, in the Controller's words?
What share of invoices, by count and by euro, have no purchase order?

tasks.short: Code invoices to the right ledger, site and VAT code.

today.trigger: An invoice is ready to book and needs a ledger, a cost centre, a site and a VAT code.
steps: See whether the creditor card already has a default ledger and VAT code.
Read the PDF for the site, the cost type and any reverse-charge wording.
Pick the code from memory or from last month's similar invoice.
Type the code on the AFAS line.
Ask a colleague when the split between warehouse and transport is unclear.
drudgery: Looking up the same supplier coding again
Guessing the site from a vague invoice description
Reworking codes the Accountant changes at month end
today.time_sinks: Invoices that cover more than one site, and agency invoices where the fee, the wages and the expenses want different ledgers. The written procedure is thin, so the three bookkeepers keep the real rules in their heads.

lenses.faster: A supplier with a signed default is coded as the invoice is captured. The bookkeeper spends time only on new suppliers and on lines that break the default.
lenses.autonomous: When a known supplier invoice matches its own rule, the code is applied as soon as capture finishes, with no reminder to code the pile.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every line, including the small carrier bills people rush today, would carry the right site cost centre in the week it arrived, so the forecast is not repaired at close.
lenses.joy: Hunting for last month's code is work nobody will miss. Choosing the treatment of a one-off damage settlement is the part people still want to make.
lenses.options: For a line the rule does not know, show up to five codes from that supplier's history, each with the site and VAT code that went with it.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the coding rules per supplier and reviews the lines that fell through, one layer above coding each document.
reach: The reclasses the Accountant now posts at close because the site or the ledger was wrong.
A cleaner split of agency cost for the FP&A Analyst, who now cannot see fee versus passed-through wages.
Cost questions from site managers that are really 'which code did you use'.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing that waiting hours at Rotterdam belong on that site's transport cost centre, and that a German carrier's invoice is reverse charge. Those distinctions are only partly written down.
tasks.pattern_why: The invoice text is unstructured. The code is a small set of fields that can be checked against the chart of accounts and the VAT list. The model proposes; the rule table accepts or rejects. Volume is not high enough, on the scores for this task, to let new patterns through unattended.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice has been captured and has no signed coding rule, or a line disagrees with the supplier default.
steps: Read the description, the supplier country and any VAT wording on the PDF.
Propose ledger, cost centre, site and VAT code from the creditor card and the last year of postings.
Reject a proposal that is not on the chart of accounts or the VAT list.
Show the bookkeeper the proposal and the closest historical codes.
On approval, offer to save the choice as the supplier rule so the next identical invoice does not ask again.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves each new or changed supplier rule. The Controller signs the VAT defaults. An invoice that matches a signed rule posts its code without a fresh approval.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and cost centres per site
VAT code list, including reverse charge and intra-community
At least a year of posted lines per creditor
The creditor card defaults already stored in AFAS
Agency contract structure: fee, passed-through wages, expenses
in_practice.logs_to: The creditor card in AFAS for the live default, and a short rule-change log on SharePoint so the Accountant can see who changed a code and when.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds a default ledger account and VAT code on the creditor card and uses them on the next purchase invoice.
Vic.ai suggests a general-ledger code from prior invoices of the same supplier.
Whether a suggestion will respect Noordhaven's three sites and reverse-charge transport bills is untested.

risks: A wrong site cost centre makes the Power BI site result and the forecast quietly wrong.
A reverse-charge invoice coded as 21 percent VAT creates a filing error.
A model copies last month's wrong code forward and the error becomes the new default.
Agency invoices can contain named workers and rates; the coding screen must not become a place those names are copied into Teams.
research_questions: Are the coding rules written on SharePoint, or do they sit with the three bookkeepers?
What share of lines, by count and by euro, repeats a supplier, ledger, cost centre and VAT combination from the last six months?
How often does the Accountant recode during close, and which ledgers move?
Does the creditor card in this AFAS administration already hold a default ledger, cost centre and VAT code?

today.trigger: A payment run, a customer receipt, a lease instalment or a question about what is still open.
steps: Read the open item and the payment terms in AFAS.
Work out the balance, the early-payment discount or the interest in Excel when AFAS does not show it.
Check VAT on the base before the discount.
Apply a partial payment across invoices when a customer paid one lump sum.
Type the result back into the payment proposal or the answer.
drudgery: Rebuilding a balance AFAS already holds because the Excel sheet is the one people trust
Hand-working interest day counts
Splitting one bank amount across several invoices on a calculator
today.time_sinks: Partial payments and the few contracts with a real discount or an interest clause. Most suppliers are simply 30 days, so the Excel work is uneven and easy to get wrong at the cent, which then blocks the bank match.

lenses.faster: Balance, discount, VAT on the discounted base and late-payment interest are filled from the invoice date and the term table. The side spreadsheet goes away.
lenses.autonomous: Creating a payment proposal or matching a customer receipt calculates the open amount and any discount that is still inside its window.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the contractual discount, the interest clause and the agency fee percentage would be applied to every invoice, including the small ones that are not worth half an hour in Excel today.
lenses.joy: Day-count interest on a calculator is work nobody will miss. The choice to waive interest for a customer a site wants to keep is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: For each payment run, show three figures per supplier that offers a discount: pay this week and take the discount, pay on the due date, or pay late with the contract interest, all in euro.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the term table per supplier and customer and checks that AFAS and any leftover sheet agree, one layer above doing the arithmetic.
reach: The cash-timing lines the FP&A Analyst now estimates.
The interest amount on a reminder the Credit and Collections Officer now calculates.
Lease balance checks the Accountant keeps for truck and equipment contracts.

tasks.human_edge: Waiving interest, taking a discount that would strain a small carrier, and reading a one-off settlement clause that is not in the term table. The arithmetic itself does not need a person.
tasks.pattern_why: Amounts due, discounts, balances and interest are dates and rates. The result can be recomputed to the cent. Once the terms sit in a table, a model adds nothing.

in_practice.trigger: A payment proposal is created, a customer receipt is matched, or a lease instalment falls due.
steps: Read due date, discount window, discount percent and interest rate from the creditor or debtor card.
Compute the open balance, the discount if the run date is inside the window, and the VAT on the right base.
Split a lump-sum receipt across open invoices by the rule the Controller has signed, oldest first unless a reference says otherwise.
Compute statutory or contract interest only when the card says interest is chargeable.
Park a result the term table cannot produce, such as a settlement figure, for the bookkeeper.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper confirms before a discount is taken or interest is invoiced. A plain balance used inside AFAS needs no separate sign-off.
data_needed: Payment terms, discount percent and discount days on the creditor and debtor cards
Contract interest rate where one exists
The statutory commercial rate and its start date, if finance ever charges it
Open items and partial payments already matched
Lease schedules with principal and interest split
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS open item, which stores the calculated discount or interest as a field the nightly extract can show next to the invoice.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit calculates open-item balances, VAT and due dates from the invoice and the payment condition.
Early-payment discount and late-payment interest are date arithmetic on those same fields.
The Dutch statutory commercial interest rate is a published rate and can be applied with a formula; AFAS does not replace the decision to charge it.

risks: Interest counted from the wrong date, invoice date versus receipt date versus agreed due date, starts a dispute with a customer.
A discount is taken that the supplier did not offer, or one the contract allows is missed.
Cent rounding leaves residuals that the bank match will not clear.
The agency fee is a percentage on a wage base; the wrong base misstates the cost of the flex pool.
research_questions: Which calculations are still done in Excel, and how many times a week?
Do the supplier and customer cards hold discount and interest, or only a 30-day term?
How often is the amount paid different from the invoice amount, and for which reason?
Is late interest ever invoiced, or only worked out and then waived?

tasks.short: Prepare the payment run for suppliers, tax and utilities.

today.trigger: The scheduled payment run, or a due date for VAT, energy or a tax payment the Accountant has calculated.
steps: Select due, approved creditor items in AFAS and drop disputed ones by hand.
Check the total, the discount and the IBAN on the proposal.
Export the SEPA file and upload it in Rabobank.
Ask the second authoriser to sign.
Pay a few items, often the tax office, as a single transfer when they are not in the batch.
drudgery: Clicking invoices into the proposal one hold at a time
Retyping an amount or an IBAN for a one-off transfer
Chasing the second authoriser because the file was ready late
today.time_sinks: The run itself is concentrated on one or two days a week, and it slips when holds are unclear or a supplier has sent a new IBAN in the same week. Utilities are often direct debit, so they surprise cash without ever sitting in the batch.

lenses.faster: The due items, the holds and the SEPA total are ready when the bookkeeper opens the run. Building the file by hand shrinks to a review.
lenses.autonomous: On the agreed weekdays AFAS assembles a proposal from approved, matched, undisputed invoices, including utilities and tax amounts that are already on the calendar.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost small carriers would be paid on the contract day in the peak season, and energy direct debits would show in the same cash view before they hit Rabobank.
lenses.joy: Retyping IBANs into the bank is work nobody will miss. The short review with the second signer is the part people treat as the real control, and it stays.
lenses.options: Three versions of the same run: everything due, everything due except disputes and agency invoices on hold, and a cash-capped version under a limit the Controller sets.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets the run calendar and the rules for what may enter a batch, and reviews what the rules excluded, one layer above preparing each payment.
reach: The week-ahead cash leaving the account, which the FP&A Analyst now pieces together.
Tax payment dates the Controller tracks on a side list.
A paid-or-not answer the Credit and Collections Officer needs when a customer points at a missing credit.

tasks.human_edge: The second signature, the choice to hold a supplier because of a dispute or a missing credit note, and any payment to a new IBAN. Liability for the money sits with the people who release the batch in Rabobank.
tasks.pattern_why: Selecting and totalling a batch is rules. Releasing money is a two-person act. The batch can be prepared on a schedule; it does not leave AFAS for Rabobank until both authorisers have signed.

in_practice.trigger: The payment calendar hits a run day, or a VAT, wage-tax or utility due date that finance is responsible for paying.
steps: List approved open items due on or before the run date, with discount and hold flags applied.
Split out any creditor whose IBAN changed since the last payment.
Show the three batch totals: full, excluding holds, and under the Controller's cash cap.
The bookkeeper reviews holds, disputes and new IBANs; the second authoriser reviews the total and the tax and utility lines.
AFAS sends the SEPA file, both sign in Rabobank, and the returned status marks the items paid.
in_practice.human_gate: No file is uploaded until two authorised people have approved that batch. A new IBAN is checked against a known source and never rides in an unattended file. Wage-tax amounts stay as payroll calculated them.
data_needed: Approved open payables with due dates and holds
IBAN history on the creditor
Dispute flags
The tax payment calendar and the amount the Accountant or Payroll Specialist has already calculated
Which utilities are direct debit rather than batch payments
Authoriser limits in Rabobank
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS payment journal together with the Rabobank batch reference, filed in the month-close folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit builds a payment proposal from open creditor items and exports a SEPA payment file.
Rabobank business banking accepts SEPA batches and supports more than one authoriser on a business account.
A cash-capped second version of the same run is a filter on the open items, not a separate banking product.

risks: A changed IBAN on a supplier invoice is the usual fraud path; an unattended batch would pay it.
One person both builds and signs if the Rabobank limits are loose.
Energy and lease direct debits bypass the batch and surprise the cash forecast.
A disputed agency invoice is paid because the hold flag was never set.
A tax payment goes out with the wrong Belastingdienst payment reference.
research_questions: How many payment runs are there per week, and how long from selection to the second Rabobank signature?
What share of euro paid last quarter was SEPA batch, direct debit, or a one-off transfer?
How is a changed supplier IBAN checked today, and who may change it in AFAS?
Who are the Rabobank authorisers, and above which amount is a second signature required?

tasks.short: Match AFAS against the bank and the side lists.

today.trigger: The bank statement is in, or someone asks whether the Excel list for a site, a fuel card or an agency still agrees with AFAS.
steps: Import or open the Rabobank statement in AFAS.
Let AFAS suggest matches, then clear the ones that are obvious by hand.
Open the Excel side list and tick lines against a print or an export.
Note breaks: missing invoice, lump-sum payment, bank fee, wrong debtor.
Leave the unexplained lines for the Accountant at close.
drudgery: Ticking a statement against a screen
Rebuilding an Excel list that is a copy of AFAS
Hunting a reference that was shortened on the bank line
today.time_sinks: The last days of the month, when unmatched bank lines and a stale agency or fuel-card sheet hold up the close. Split payments, one amount covering several invoices, take the longest.

lenses.faster: Bank lines, AFAS open items and the Excel side lists match on amount, date and reference. Ticking a printout disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Each morning after the CAMT.053 import, the match runs and only breaks are waiting. The nightly extract refreshes the dashboard afterwards.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every agency statement and every fuel-card list would be matched in the same week, and the side journals people still keep would be retired once the match is trusted.
lenses.joy: Ticking paper or Excel against AFAS is work nobody will miss. A break that means a missing invoice or a payment on the wrong debtor is the part worth a person's attention.
lenses.options: For an unmatched bank line, show the closest open items by amount, supplier and date, up to five, and leave the line unmatched until one is chosen.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper decides which side lists are still allowed to exist and tightens the match rules, one layer above performing the comparison.
reach: The reconciliation workpapers the Accountant assembles for the close.
The cash position the FP&A Analyst needs before the forecast is updated.
Unmatched receipts the Credit and Collections Officer would otherwise chase as if they were still open.

tasks.human_edge: Reading a break that is a real event: one payment for two invoices, a Rabobank fee, a deposit that belongs to payroll, or a short payment tied to a damage claim. The match rule cannot explain those.
tasks.pattern_why: Both sides are lists of amounts, dates and references. Matching is rules plus a cent tolerance. The output is matched, or a break with a reason, and it can be recomputed without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Rabobank's CAMT.053 is imported, or a side list is dropped in SharePoint: agency statement, fuel cards, or a site cash sheet.
steps: Normalise the bank file or the side list to amount, date, reference and counterparty.
Match to AFAS open items on amount, IBAN or debtor, invoice reference and a short date window.
Clear unique matches inside the cent tolerance.
Propose near matches for split payments and for a single payment that equals a batch total.
Put the remaining breaks on the bookkeeper's list for the close pack.
in_practice.human_gate: A break is not force-matched. Writing off a residual above the Controller's threshold waits for the Accountant.
data_needed: CAMT.053 bank lines
AFAS open items with invoice references
Agency and fuel-card exports
The list of Excel journals that still exist and who owns each
The write-off threshold the Controller already uses
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS matching log, and a break report on the Power BI finance dashboard after the nightly refresh.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit matches imported bank statement lines to open creditor and debtor items.
Rabobank delivers CAMT.053 statements for business accounts.
BlackLine compares two account lists and records a person's sign-off on the breaks.

risks: Matching on amount alone clears the wrong invoice when many bills share a round amount, such as rent or a repeated shuttle.
A side list that is weeks behind looks like an AFAS error and sends the bookkeeper hunting in the wrong place.
Retiring a site's Excel sheet without agreeing what replaces it for that site.
The Power BI page is a nightly extract, so a same-day match is invisible there until the next refresh.
research_questions: Which journals are still kept in Excel, by whom, and why are they outside AFAS?
What share of bank lines match automatically today, and what are the top break reasons?
Do the agency portals and the fuel-card provider give a line export, or a PDF?
What residual is the Controller already willing to write off without the Accountant?

tasks.short: Look up an account and answer the question.

today.trigger: A site manager, a supplier, an FP&A colleague or the Credit and Collections Officer asks what happened to an invoice or a balance.
steps: Read the mail or the Teams message and find the supplier, customer or invoice number.
Open the creditor or debtor in AFAS and check open items, payments and the dossier.
Export to Excel when the question is a period or a cost centre rather than one invoice.
Write a short reply, often in Dutch, with the figure and the next payment date.
Chase a colleague when the item sits in someone else's unposted batch.
drudgery: Interrupting the posting work to answer 'have we paid this'
Re-exporting a cost-centre list that the nightly dashboard might already hold
Repeating the same answer to a new site supervisor
today.time_sinks: The questions bunch up at month end and just after the payment run. Cost-centre questions take longer than single invoices because the answer is assembled from the extract, not from one screen.

lenses.faster: Open items, last payment and invoice status come back as soon as the question names a supplier, a customer or an invoice number. Screen-hopping and a fresh Excel export drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A Teams or mailbox question that contains an invoice number creates a draft answer with the AFAS fields attached, without a reminder to process the inbox.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every site lead would read their own open orders, accruals and cost-centre spend, and the bookkeeper would only take the questions that screen cannot answer.
lenses.joy: Pulling a balance on demand is the interruption nobody will miss. A disputed shipment, where the number is only the start of the question, is the conversation worth having.
lenses.options: For 'why is this not paid', show the status plus the concrete reasons that fit the item: not approved, on hold, no receipt, or included in the next run date.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper turns the questions people actually ask into tiles on the finance dashboard, and keeps the ones the dashboard cannot answer.
reach: The simpler AFAS pulls the FP&A Analyst does for a site's actuals.
Debtor status the Credit and Collections Officer looks up before a call.
Account breakdowns the Accountant is asked for outside the close.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a figure from the ledger is the wrong thing to send: a customer in a dispute, a supplier about to stop a delivery, or a number a site lead will use in an argument. External mail still goes out under the bookkeeper's name.
tasks.pattern_why: The question arrives as free text, usually in Dutch. The useful output is a handful of fields from AFAS: balance, due date, last payment, hold reason. Those fields can be checked. The model reads the question; the figure comes from the query.

in_practice.trigger: An email or a Teams message asks about an invoice, a supplier, a customer or a cost centre.
steps: Identify the creditor, debtor, invoice or cost centre named in the question.
Query AFAS for a single account, or the nightly extract when the question is a period total.
Attach the source lines to a short Dutch draft that quotes only those figures and the next payment-run date.
Send external replies only after the bookkeeper has read them. After a trial month, internal balance questions can return on Teams with the source link.
Log the question type so repeated ones can be added to the dashboard.
in_practice.human_gate: Any reply to a supplier, a customer or an agency is sent by the bookkeeper. Figures that sit in an unposted batch are labelled as not yet in the ledger. Wage detail inside an agency invoice is not quoted back to a site channel.
data_needed: Open items, payment status, approval and hold flags
Cost-centre balances from the nightly extract
The extract's last refresh time
Who is allowed to receive an external answer
A mask on agency lines that contain a worker's name or rate
in_practice.logs_to: A question log on SharePoint, with type, account and asker, reviewed monthly with the Controller.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit shows open items, payments and dossier documents for a single creditor or debtor.
Power BI can publish the nightly AFAS extract so an authorised reader can filter a cost centre without asking finance.
A Dutch draft that quotes only retrieved figures still needs a check that no extra number was added.

risks: An answer from the nightly extract is a day old, and someone chases a customer who paid this morning.
The draft states a figure that was not in the query result.
A cost question about flex workers exposes names or rates from an agency invoice in a wide Teams channel, which is an AVG problem.
Broader AFAS rights for site managers show ledger detail they should not have.
research_questions: What are the twenty most common questions in a month, and who asks them?
How many of those can the current Power BI finance dashboards already answer?
How often is the nightly extract late or different from AFAS on the next morning?
Which answers go outside the company, and who is allowed to send them today?

tasks.short: Check that customer and supplier payments are on time.

today.trigger: A debtor might be late, a lease instalment might have failed, or someone asks whether Noordhaven itself has paid on time.
steps: Export open debtors and creditors from AFAS to Excel.
Age them against 30 days or the card terms.
Mark disputes and promised dates if they are known.
Send the worst debtors to the Credit and Collections Officer.
Check lease or loan instalments from the Accountant's schedule when it is close week.
drudgery: Rebuilding the ageing pivot each week
Finding out by mail whether a late item is a dispute
Scanning for missed outgoing payments only when a supplier complains
today.time_sinks: The list is rebuilt rather than watched. Small overdue amounts wait while the large ones are chased, which is where days sales outstanding quietly grow. Lease schedules that live outside AFAS are checked late.

lenses.faster: Each morning the bookkeeper gets customers and suppliers past their terms, with the amount and the number of days, and does not rebuild the ageing in Excel.
lenses.autonomous: The list refreshes when the bank match posts a receipt and again when a due date passes unpaid.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every debtor, every lease instalment and every agency prepayment would be watched daily, so small overdue amounts are seen while they can still move days sales outstanding.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the ageing workbook is work nobody will miss. Deciding which late account is a real dispute, and which customer has gone quiet, is the judgment people still want.
lenses.options: Three views of the same book: everything past terms, only amounts large enough to move days sales outstanding, and lease or loan instalments due in the next two weeks.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper keeps the definition of on time, terms, grace days and dispute codes, and hands the Credit and Collections Officer a list that is already split.
reach: Queue preparation for the Credit and Collections Officer, who now starts from a raw export.
The cash-in assumption in the FP&A forecast.
The days-sales-outstanding figure the Controller reports, fed from the same open items.

tasks.human_edge: Telling a dispute or a promised payment from simple lateness, and holding a reminder while commercial colleagues renegotiate. A cancelled direct-debit mandate on a lease is visible only to someone who knows that contract.
tasks.pattern_why: On time is a comparison of due date, terms, open amount and the last matched payment. The output is a list with days overdue. Producing the list does not need a model. Sending a reminder stays with the Credit and Collections Officer.

in_practice.trigger: Each morning after the bank match, and as soon as a due date passes with an open balance.
steps: Age open debtors and unpaid creditor items against the terms on the card.
Flag lease and loan instalments that are due or missed, once those schedules sit in AFAS.
Split debtors into dispute, promise to pay, and no contact yet.
Give the debtor list to the Credit and Collections Officer. Keep missed outgoing payments with the bookkeeper.
Publish overdue totals and days sales outstanding on the finance Power BI dashboard from the nightly extract.
in_practice.human_gate: Reminders go out from the Credit and Collections Officer. The bookkeeper contacts a supplier only when Noordhaven is the late party and a delivery or a release of goods is at risk.
data_needed: Open items with due dates
Dispute and promise-to-pay flags
Customer and supplier payment terms
Lease and loan instalment schedules
The days-sales-outstanding definition the Finance Director already uses
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI finance dashboard the Controller reviews, plus a short overdue list in the month-close pack.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit keeps debtor and creditor open items and can produce reminder runs from due dates.
HighRadius monitors open receivables and ranks accounts that are past due.
A page on the nightly extract will lag AFAS by a day whenever a large receipt is matched this morning.

risks: A reminder to a customer with a real damage claim on a shipment makes the commercial relationship worse.
Two definitions of days sales outstanding, one in AFAS and one in the FP&A model, make the dashboard argue with the forecast.
A lease or loan schedule that stays in the Accountant's file is invisible to the morning list.
Agency prepayments follow a different rhythm from ordinary 30-day suppliers and will look falsely overdue.
research_questions: Is the ageing built in AFAS or in Excel today, and how many hours a week does it take?
What share of overdue debtors are disputes, and who sets the dispute flag?
Are lease and loan schedules in AFAS or in a file the Accountant keeps?
Which days-sales-outstanding definition does the Finance Director already trust?

role.altitude: The bookkeeper becomes the owner of the accounts-payable and accounts-receivable rules: what may post, what may be paid, which codes are allowed, and which breaks the close still has to see. The three people keep that queue small enough that the month is matched before the Accountant starts.
reach: Routine bank and subledger reconciliations that now sit with the Accountant.
The overdue list and the plain account-status answers the Credit and Collections Officer now builds by hand.
A week-ahead figure of cash leaving Rabobank, taken from the approved payment batches, for the FP&A Analyst.
The untouched-invoice, uncoded-invoice and unmatched-bank counts the Controller uses as close controls.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 37 percent of the role, roughly 580 hours a year for each of the three people. Keying, ticking and rebuilding Excel can shrink a long way. The hours that remain are the exceptions and the dual sign-off: agency invoices that do not match approved hours, transport bills with no purchase order, a changed IBAN, VAT that is not the supplier default, and disputes. Rabobank still needs two human authorisers. Accruals, supplier calls and audit samples sit outside this list and stay person-sized. A peak of 300 flex workers is absorbable with the same three people only when the agencies deliver line-level hours, not a single PDF.
skills_to_grow: Writing coding and match rules the Controller can sign, including VAT for domestic, reverse-charge and intra-community invoices.
Reading a SEPA batch and a bank break list, and explaining a break in the close meeting.
Tracking straight-through rate, invoices processed without touch, and days to close, and turning a worse week into a rule change.
Setting AFAS and dashboard rights so a site sees its costs while worker names and rates on agency invoices stay covered.
role.ambitious_version: Routine supplier, utility and agency invoices are in AFAS the week they arrive, matched to Rabobank, and paid on the contract day under the same two-person sign-off. The three bookkeepers spend the week on holds, disputes, new IBANs and the VAT lines the rules refuse. The Accountant inherits a matched ledger, so days to close move. The forecast sits closer to the truth because each site's cost centres were coded the same way all month, including the weeks the flex pool climbs toward 300. The peak is carried by the same three people, and the Credit and Collections Officer and the Accountant receive a ready list and a ready reconciliation.
